title: SpaceXAI’s Grok programming tool was uploading its users’ entire codebase to cloud storage
slides: Your codebase secretly uploaded to the cloud?
Grok sent entire projects without asking.
Not just snippets—every file, folder, and config.
Stop trusting auto-upload; audit every tool now.
One rule: never let AI see code it doesn't need.
thread_text:
1. Your codebase in the cloud?

Grok sent entire projects to the cloud without asking—no prompt, no alert, just auto-upload.

2. Not just snippets

Every file, folder, and config file was uploaded. No filter for sensitive credentials or API keys.

3. Auto-upload by default

Many tools now enable background sync silently. You never gave consent for full project transfer.

4. Audit every tool now

Check your IDE, terminal, and AI plugins. One misconfigured setting leaks your entire repo.

5. Simulate this today

Open a fresh project in your AI tool, watch network traffic. Does it send files you didn't approve?

instagram.caption:
Your entire codebase got uploaded to a cloud server—every file, folder, and config—without you ever clicking "send." 🚨

Grok, SpaceXAI's programming tool, silently synced whole projects by default. No prompt, no alert for your API keys or passwords inside.

This means your private work, credentials, and proprietary logic are now sitting on a third-party server you never authorized. 🗂️

If you use any AI coding assistant, open a fresh project and watch your network traffic right now—what is it sending without asking? 🔍
